metadata.methods_description: Cue-based left- vs right-hand motor imagery paradigm in stroke patients, where one hand is paretic and the other unaffected. EEG was recorded from 63 channels at 512 Hz with 50 Hz line frequency, in one session of two runs per subject, 40 trials per class, with trial interval 0-6.8 s. Data are preprocessed and epoched.

citation_details.abstract: Stroke is a leading cause of death and disability worldwide, significantly impairing motor and cognitive functions. Effective rehabilitation is often hindered by the heterogeneity of stroke lesions, variability in recovery patterns, and the complexity of electroencephalography (EEG) signals, which are often contaminated by artifacts. citation_details.author: Xiangkai Wang, Zhao Yun, Dongyi He, Qingling Xia, Gen Li, Xinlai Xing, Yuchi Pan, Bin Jiang
citation_details.abstract: Motor imagery electroencephalography (MI-EEG) decoding offers a non-invasive route for post-stroke rehabilitation, but cross-patient use remains difficult because pathological neural reorganization changes task-related EEG dynamics, aperiodic activity, local excitability, cross-regional coordination, and trial-level brain-state context. This makes source-learned MI representations unreliable for unseen patients. To address this problem, we propose CFSPMNet, a cross-patient adaptation framework that models post-stroke MI-EEG as latent neural-state organization. citation_details.author: Xiangkai Wang, Zhao Yun, Dongyi He, Qingling Xia, Gen Li, Nizhuan Wang, Ningxiao Peng, Bin Jiang
citation_details.abstract: Stroke patient cross-subject electroencephalography (EEG) decoding of motor imagery (MI) brain-computer interface (BCI) is essential for motor rehabilitation, yet lesion-related abnormal temporal dynamics and pronounced inter-patient heterogeneity often undermine generalization. citation_details.title: An Explainable Biomarker-Driven Neuroadaptive Framework for Upper-Limb Stroke Rehabilitation Using Eeg Motor Imagery
citation_details.author: Arthi T, Sumathy G
citation_details.venue: International Conference Computational Vision and Bio Inspired Computing
citation_details.abstract: Upper-limb motor impairment affects most stroke survivors, motivating the development of adaptive, interpretable, and clinically meaningful rehabilitation systems. This paper proposes an explainable biomarker-driven neuroadaptive framework for upper-limb stroke rehabilitation using electroencephalogram (EEG)-based motor imagery (MI). The framework integrates label-independent EEG biomarker extraction, statistical feature selection, comparative MI decoding, and a Neurofunctional Readiness Index (NRI) to map biomarker evidence into four adaptive virtual reality (VR) rehabilitation tiers. Performance was evaluated using leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) crossvalidation on a publicly available acute-stroke MI-EEG dataset comprising 15 subjects, 63 EEG channels, and 1,200 trials.
